title: Reshape Nevada Warranty Data to Interval Censored Format
varMonth: Select the production/shipment month column (cohort label)
varShipQty: Select the units shipped / delivered (ShipQty) column
varFailCols: Select ALL failure-count columns in chronological order (earliest month first)
labelDateFormats: Date format settings - tell the module how your dates are stored
monthColFormat: Production Month column format (the values in the Month column you selected above)
hdrFormat: Failure column header format (the column names of the failure columns selected above)
newdatasetname: New dataset name for the reshaped (interval-censored) output
sortOrder: Sort output by Age_L: ascending (default) or descending
labelInfo: Nevada table: rows = shipment cohorts, columns = failure counts per calendar month. Output has one row per unit with Age_L, Age_U, and Status (1=failed, 0=censored).
labelColNote: IMPORTANT: select the failure columns in strict chronological order (earliest month first). The column position determines the age-interval assigned to each failure.
labelDateNote: IMPORTANT: select the format that matches EXACTLY how dates appear in your data. If your Month column is already a Date/POSIXct type (converted via Variables > Convert menu), select 'Date/POSIXct (already converted)'.

help.title: Reshape Nevada Warranty Data
help.body:
Description

Converts a Nevada (warranty matrix) table into a one-row-per-unit interval-censored dataset ready for Parametric Survival Analysis (Interval).

Input format
  • Month column - cohort label (production or shipment month). Can be YYYYMM integer, MMM-YY, Date/POSIXct, or other supported formats.
  • ShipQty column - total units shipped / delivered in that cohort.
  • Failure columns - one column per observation calendar month, containing the count of new failures observed in that month for that cohort. Select them in chronological order (left to right).
Date format settings
You must specify the format for two separate elements:
  1. Production Month column format - the format of the values inside the Month column you selected (e.g. 202501 or Jan-25).
  2. Failure column header format - the format of the column names themselves (e.g. 202502, Jan-25).
Both are converted internally to a YYYYMM integer for arithmetic. The difference between consecutive months gives each cohort its correct observation span (Age_L for survivors).

Supported formats
  • YYYYMM - e.g. 202501 (six-digit integer, no separator)
  • MMM-YY - e.g. Jan-25 (three-letter month, two-digit year)
  • MMM-YYYY - e.g. Jan-2025 (three-letter month, four-digit year)
  • YYYY-MM - e.g. 2025-01 (ISO format with hyphen)
  • MM/YYYY - e.g. 01/2025 (month slash year)
  • Date/POSIXct - already a proper R date (converted via BlueSky Data > Convert)
  • Age index (1, 2, 3 ...) - columns are age numbers not calendar dates; positional fallback logic is used for survivor Age_L
Output columns
  • Age_L - lower age bound in months.
  • Age_U - upper age bound in months (Inf for survivors).
  • Status - 1 = failed, 0 = right-censored survivor.
  • Month - original cohort label, retained for stratification.
Validation output
After reshaping, a Survivor Age_L by Cohort table is printed. Age_L should decrease for more recently shipped cohorts. If all cohorts show the same Age_L the date format selection is likely wrong.

Next step
Open Warranty Parametric Survival (Interval) and select Age_L as Start time (L) and Age_U as End time (U).
